text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Prime Minister Abdul Salam al-Majali departs to the United States to join King Hussein in next week's talks in Washington; says hopes the U.S. would fulfill its obligations towards Jordan.
- Confessions of the Jordanian soldier who gunned the Israeli schoolgirls this month points to an individual act committed on the "spur of the moment", legal sources say.
- Jordan says it wants to contain damage to the Middle East peace process of the Israeli settlement drive in Arab East Jerusalem.
- Lawyer defending the Jordanian soldier who gunned Israel schoolgirls says the girls mocked him while praying; expects charges list expected in a few days after completion of the interrogation.

- PM Majali, in comments before his departure to the U.S., says the peace process was faltering on all fronts and "the economic situation is difficult and we hope the U.S. will provide aid to Jordan."
